task_payload.text:
A factory produces two types of food, I and II, and currently has 50 skilled workers. It is known that one skilled worker can produce $10 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food I or $6 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food II. According to contract bookings, the weekly demand for these two foods will rise sharply, as shown in Table 1-11. Therefore, the factory has decided to train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week. It is known that a worker works $40 \ \mathrm{h}$ per week, and a skilled worker can train up to three new workers in two weeks (during the training period, both the skilled worker and the trainees do not participate in production). The weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan, the weekly wage of a trainee during the training period is 120 yuan, and after training, the wage is 240 yuan per week, with the same production efficiency as skilled workers. During the transition period of training, many skilled workers are willing to work overtime, and the factory has decided to arrange some workers to work $60 \ \mathrm{h} per week, with a weekly wage of 540 yuan. If the booked food cannot be delivered on time, the compensation fee for each week of delay per kg is 0.5 yuan for food I and 0.6 yuan for food II. Under these conditions, how should the factory make comprehensive arrangements to minimize the total cost?

steps: Define integer decision variables: t1 = number of jets allocated to training in year 1 (0..10), t2 = number of jets allocated to training in year 2 (0..15).

Year 2 jets start training in year 2; after 1 year they have 5*t2 pilots HALF-trained (not fully trained until year 3).

Alternative interpretation: total trained (including partial) = 50 + 5*t2. With t2=15 (all jets train): 50 + 75 = 125.

task_payload.text:
The contract reservations for the next year for products I, II, and III of a certain factory in each quarter are shown in Table 1-10.

Table 1-10
| Product | 1    | 2    | 3    | 4    |
|---------|------|------|------|------|
| I       | 1500 | 1000 | 2000 | 1200 |
| II      | 1500 | 1500 | 1200 | 1500 |
| III     | 1000 | 2000 | 1500 | 2500 |

At the beginning of the first quarter, there is no inventory for these three products, and it is required to have 150 units in stock for each product by the end of the fourth quarter. It is known that the factory has 15,000 production hours per quarter, and each unit of products I, II, and III requires 2, 4, and 3 hours respectively. Due to a change in equipment, product I cannot be produced in the second quarter. It is stipulated that if the products cannot be delivered on time, a compensation of 20 yuan per unit per quarter delay is required for products I and II, while for product III, the compensation is 10 yuan. Additionally, for products produced but not delivered in the current quarter, the inventory cost is 5 yuan per unit per quarter. How should the factory schedule production to minimize the total cost of compensation and inventory?

method.name: milp_production_inventory_backlog
steps: Define integer production variables for each product (I,II,III) in each quarter (Q1-Q4), non-negative inventory variables, and non-negative backlog variables.
Capacity constraint per quarter: 2*prod_I[q] + 4*prod_II[q] + 3*prod_III[q] <= 15000.
Zero production for product I in Q2.
Inventory balance: inv[p,q] = inv[p,q-1] + prod[p,q] - demand[p,q] + backlog[p,q-1] - backlog[p,q]. Initial inv at Q1 start = 0.

Backlog penalty accumulated: each unit of backlog at end of quarter q has been delayed q quarters, so total backlog delay cost = 20*(1*bl[I,Q1]+2*bl[I,Q2]+3*bl[I,Q3]+4*bl[I,Q4]) + same pattern for II + 10*(1*bl[III,Q1]+...+4*bl[III,Q4]).
Holding cost: 5*sum over all inv[p,q].
Final inventory >= 150 for each product at end of Q4.
Use HiGHS high-level API (addVariable/addConstr/getSolution) to solve as MILP with integer production variables.
